div.l: That were of lawe exꝑperrt ⁊and corious
Of whiche þere were a doseyn īn that hous
Worthi to ben styward of rente ⁊and lond
Of ony lord that is in yngelond
To make hȳm lyue / by his owene good
In honour detteles but he werere wod
Or leue as skarsely as hȳm liste desire
And able for to helpȳn al a schyre
In ony cas that myȝte falle or happe
And ȝit this maūnsiple / sette and here allerys cappe
The reue was a sclendere colerik manA Reve
Hese berd was schaue as nygh as eủere he can
His her was by hese erys ful roude I schorn
His top was dokkyd as a pryst be forn
Ful longe were hese leggis ⁊and ful lene
Y lik a staf ther was no calf I sene
Wel couthe he kepe a gerner ⁊and a bȳnne
There non auditour couthe on hȳm wȳnne
Wel wiste he be þe droute ⁊and be the reyn
The ȝildynge of hese sed ⁊and of hese greyn
His lordis schep hese net hese deyerye
Hese swyn hese hors hese stoor ⁊and his pultrie
Was holly in þis revis gouernȳnge
And be þe couenaūnt ȝaf the rekenȳnge
Sȳn þat his lord was twenty ȝer of age
The coude no man brȳngȳn hȳn in a rerage
Ther nas bayle herde ne oþ̉er hyne
That he knew his sleythe ⁊and conynge
The were adred of hym as of the deþ
Hese wonyng was ful fayre / vp on an heth
With grene treis I schadewid was hese place
He couthe betere þan hese lord purchase
Ful riche he was a storid preuyly
Hese lord. wel couthe he plese subtily
To ȝeue ⁊and lene hȳm of hese owene good
And haue a thank ⁊and ȝit a cote and hood.
